text:
alex: Hey team, escalated from Customer Success — enterprise customer (org: AcmeRetail) seeing a big spike of 504 / gateway timeouts since ~09:30 PDT. They started seeing ~40-60% of requests failing. They upgraded to our JS SDK v1.12 yesterday.

support-bot: New ticket created: #INC-9876 — attached initial logs from customer.

maria: Thanks. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK snippet), model + region, and at least one trace-id from the 504s? Also, are these streaming requests?

alex: Customer sent this curl repro:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3.2x","input":"hello","stream":false}'
```

They said SDK uses default concurrency ~8 and they call concurrently from a lambda pool (~200 concurrent lambdas). Example failing trace-id: trace=tr_0a1b2c3d, another tr_1f2e3d4c. Region: us-west-2.

devon: I pulled gateway logs for those trace ids: we have repeated errors: 

```
2026-03-10T16:31:02Z ERROR gateway timeout waiting for runtime response route=/v1/generate model=rwd-3.2x trace=tr_0a1b2c3d status=504 backend=runtime-23
2026-03-10T16:31:03Z WARN sdk-retry request id=req_9182 attempts=3 client=acme lambda=eu-west
```

samir: Noticed a pattern: the runtime instances serving that customer are hitting high memory+swap churn right before 504s. However, another oddity: some requests show 401 from auth-service immediately prior to 504, then retries flood the gateway. Example flow: 401 -> client retry -> gateway backlog -> 504. Could be intermittent auth header truncation between customer proxy and our edge.

lena: Do we have the raw headers for failed requests? Querying logs for trace tr_0a1b2c3d shows Authorization header length = 32 for some requests and 8 for others (truncated). That would explain intermittent 401s.

maria: If the Authorization header is being truncated by their proxy or our ingress, the auth service will reject, client retries might overwhelm the runtime pool and cause timeouts. Two parallel paths to investigate: 1) why header is truncated, 2) mitigate by adding retry budget / 4xx handling in gateway to avoid retry storms.

alex: Customer says they use CloudFront + custom lambda edge that injects an x-acme-auth header and also add long cookie strings. Could be header size pushing into chunking/truncation on edge.

devon: I can reproduce header truncation locally by sending a large Cookie header + long custom header to our edge endpoint when using Nginx config with `proxy_buffer_size` low. Two actions: ask customer to check their proxy header size limits and add a temporary mitigation on our side to treat auth 401s as terminal for retries (i.e., don't auto-retry 401).

samir: Also saw in gateway metrics a spike of simultaneous connections at ~09:30 PDT matching their lambdas ramping — concurrency *and* retry amplification could explain why small auth failures escalated to 504.

maria: Quick temporary mitigation I can deploy: update gateway retry policy to not retry on 401 and to add a per-api-key token bucket to limit retry amplification for that customer. Rolling a canary now to us-west-2 only.

maria (after deploy): Canary is up — changed config `retry_on_401=false`, `retry_budget=5/sec` for org AcmeRetail. Monitoring.

oncall-bot: Canary: gateway-config/us-west-2 updated by maria at 16:45Z.

alex: Customer updated: asked them to check their edge headers and to temporarily reduce parallelism from 200 -> 40 to see if errors drop. They pushed back, want us to confirm root cause.

lena: I pulled packet logs from the edge for a failing request: raw Authorization header ends with `...sk-abc` and appears truncated after 40 bytes. Upstream (customer side) shows full token length 64. So truncation is upstream of our edge — their lambda edge is clobbering or trimming long headers when combining cookies.

devon: Repro steps I used:

1) Start a local nginx with `proxy_buffer_size 4k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 8k;` and a test backend that echoes headers.
2) Send curl with a 120 char Authorization header and a 5k Cookie.
3) Observe header truncated in backend responses ~40-80% of requests.

Command: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer verylongtoken... (120 chars)" -H "Cookie: $(python -c 'print("A"*5000)')" http://localhost:8080/echo
```

Expected: auth header preserved. Actual: sometimes truncated.

maria: Good, confirms upstream header-size handling bug. Next: customer-side remediation + our mitigation. Ask customer to increase their edge header buffer or move auth token into body (for server-to-server) or use shorter token rotation.

alex: For comms: Drafted update — "we've identified an intermittent header truncation at your edge which causes auth failures followed by retries, producing timeouts on our gateway. Temporary mitigations applied on our side. Please reduce per-invocation concurrency and increase header buffer limits; our team can whitelist your org to reduce retry amplification while you patch." Want me to send?

samir: Send it. Also include recommended SDK change: pin to v1.11 which had stricter client-side backoff and disabled aggressive retry-on-401. Provide snippet:

```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RWD_KEY, retryPolicy: { maxRetries: 2, retryOn: [ '5xx' ] } });
```

alex: Sent customer update and asked for timeline to fix their lambda edge (they estimate 24-48h). Customer replied: errors dropped to ~5% after reducing concurrency and our canary deployment.

maria: I'll keep the canary for 24h and then promote if stable. Phasing next: add a permanent rule to not retry on 401 and instrument better 4xx telemetry so we can alert faster on similar patterns.

lena: Filing follow-up action items: (1) doc for customers about header size limits and SDK best-practices, (2) permanent gateway change to avoid retry amplification on client-auth failures, (3) monitor per-org retry amplification.

support-bot: Action items created in Jira: RWD-2314, RWD-2315, RWD-2316.

alex: Closing loop here — marking incident under control; will reopen if errors return above 10% after canary ends. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
